events.objective: Characterize the symptom on settlement-service: pinpoint exact onset time of zero settlements and the start of consumer lag growth (before vs after 08:22Z report). Report settlement-service error/log signatures around onset (consumer rebalance, timeouts, poll errors, auth/DB connection errors), and whether lag growth is uniform across partitions or concentrated. Also check whether the broker/queue itself (topic produce rate, broker health metrics) changed at onset, and whether any other service's error rates or throughput degraded in the same window.

Find every change (deployments and config changes) across ALL services in the window 2026-05-12T06:00Z to 09:59Z, with timestamps and the specific settings changed. Map settlement-service's upstream and downstream dependencies (broker/topic, database, ledger/clearing, account services, trade producers) and identify shared components. Search historical incidents for prior 'consumer lag / settlements stuck' events and what the root cause and fix were.

Given the onset time identified in task a, determine whether settlement-service's dependency calls around that moment were healthy: check latency/error metrics for its DB and downstream/upstream dependencies (as mapped in task b) and whether any dependency saturated (connections, threads, CPU, disk) at or just before onset. Distinguish 'consumer stuck waiting on a slow/failing dependency' from 'consumer never receiving work' by comparing message fetch/poll metrics against processing metrics.

events.statement: Only one deployment occurred across all services in the window: order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z, author a.khan, status live (not rolled back), changing the OrderExecuted event schema ('rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2').

Only one config change occurred across all services in the window: settlement-service key 'consumer.max.poll.records' reduced from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z by m.das, described as 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes'.

settlement-service is an event consumer: it consumes from the shared kafka broker (queue-consume) and writes to the shared ledger-db (db). Kafka edges show producers order-service and payment-service (queue-produce) and consumers settlement-service and notification-service.

Shared components: kafka ("shared":true, owner platform, at least 4 services attach) and ledger-db ("shared":true, postgres) — ledger-db is written by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service, so upstream/downstream neighbours can affect settlement-service through it.

The explicit upstream query for settlement-service returned no caller edges (edges: []), so no service-level HTTP producer edge into settlement-service is recorded; producer relation is only visible via the kafka queue edges (order-service/payment-service -> kafka).

Two historical incidents match 'consumer lag / settlements stuck' symptoms but with infrastructure causes, not config/schema causes: HIST-112 (2026-02-03) root cause 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance', resolution 'Restarted consumer group'; HIST-104 (2025-11-05) root cause partition reassignment rebalancing storm.

events.description: Could not retrieve kafka/ledger-db metric names or values (no metric queries were run within budget), so it is unverified whether broker lag, partition rebalance, or ledger-db write latency changed at 07:35-07:40Z.

No caller (upstream) edges are recorded for settlement-service; the 'trade producers' relation is only inferred from kafka queue-produce edges. api-gateway->order-service/payment-service are the only explicit HTTP callers found.
Historical search returned only 2 incidents (HIST-112, HIST-104) matching lag/stuck symptoms; no precedent found for a root cause caused by consumer poll settings or producer event-schema changes.

events.answer: Across ALL services in 2026-05-12T06:00Z–09:59Z there were exactly two changes: an order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40Z, "OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity") and a settlement-service config change cfg-3004 ("consumer.max.poll.records" 500 -> 200, 07:35Z). settlement-service consumes topic(s) on the shared kafka broker from producers order-service and payment-service, and writes to the shared ledger-db (also used by order-service and portfolio-service); kafka and ledger-db are both shared components, with notification-service also consuming from kafka. Two prior incidents (HIST-112, HIST-104) show similar 'consumer lag / settlements stuck' symptoms but different causes (partition reassignment/rebalance), so they are leads only.

events.statement: settlement-service throughput collapsed in the 07:32–07:48Z window: request_rate dropped from a steady ~62–63 req/s (07:00–07:32Z) to avg 16.32 at 07:40Z, then to avg 0.41 at 07:48Z where it stayed flat (~0.40) through 09:56Z. This is the onset of zero settlements, ~40 min before the 08:22Z report.

Consumer lag on settlement-service was flat (~35–55 msg) with max ~64 through 07:38Z, then began climbing at 07:41Z (avg 410.94, max 819.95) and rose monotonically to avg 60220.76 / max 61605.53 at 09:55Z — i.e., lag growth started ~07:40Z, well before the 08:22Z report.

Earliest ERROR log signature on settlement-service is a deserialization failure at 07:42:14Z on a single partition/offset: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' (213 occurrences), followed from 07:44:51Z by poison-message retry logs 'retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences). All errors reference the same offset orders-3@8841207.

All 409 matched settlement-service WARN+ logs are ERROR level (counts_by_level ERROR:409) and every entry cites the same offset orders-3@8841207 — there are no auth, DB-connection, timeout, or consumer-rebalance error signatures, and no other partition appears. This indicates the failure is concentrated on one partition, not uniform across partitions.

settlement-service itself shows no crash/restart and no service-level error-rate anomaly: restarts stayed 0.0 across 07:00–09:56Z, and HTTP 5xx error_rate stayed ~0.2% (0.10–0.32) throughout, including after onset. The single flat error_rate metric therefore does not represent the consumer failure.

The consumer lag growth and error onset pre-date the reported_at (08:22:00Z) by ~40 minutes, so the incident was already active at ~07:40Z; the human report's guess that 'changed consumer poll settings shortly before' could only be relevant if the change occurred before ~07:40Z.

events.answer: Zero settlements/throughput collapse began between 07:38Z and 07:41Z — before the 08:22Z report — coinciding with the first ERROR at 07:42:14Z, a deserialization failure on partition orders-3@8841207 ("missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)") that was retried as a poison message and blocked that partition, causing consumer lag to climb monotonically from ~50 to 61,605 by 09:55Z. This points to a single blocked partition (concentrated, not uniform) rather than a broker or service-wide failure.

events.statement: settlement-service's DB latency to its ledger-db dependency was flat across the onset: latency_p99_ms stayed ~235-243 ms (mean 238.55) for the entire 06:30-09:59Z window, with no step at 07:40Z (07:26 avg 238.49 -> 07:40 avg 241.55 -> 08:22 avg 242.56). No dependency-side latency degradation at or just before onset.

settlement-service's DB connection pool was NOT saturated and did not change at onset: db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~6 connections (mean 5.99, max 6.78, min 5.21) throughout 06:30-09:59Z, including the 07:40Z onset bucket (avg 6.03). Its own CPU was not the blocker either given the pool never grew.

ledger-db (shared downstream dependency) showed no saturation at or before onset across all four health metrics: cpu_pct flat ~30% (mean 30.05, 07:40 avg 29.65), connections_active flat ~62 (mean 61.74, 07:40 avg 61.62), slow_queries_per_min flat ~1.0/min (mean 1.0, 07:40 avg 0.87). No connection, CPU or query-latency saturation in the database.

The kafka broker (shared queue dependency) was healthy and unchanged across onset: cpu_pct flat ~35% (mean 34.85, 07:40 avg 34.38) and messages_in_per_s steady ~2531 msg/s (07:40 avg 2513.68, max 2734.12) with no dip. The broker was still delivering messages normally at onset, i.e., the consumer was receiving/producing work rather than the broker stopping.

No ledger-db error/warn logs exist in the incident window: query of ledger-db WARN+ logs for 07:30-09:59Z returned total_matched 0 with an empty counts_by_level (data range 04:00-09:59Z), so the shared database emitted no warnings/errors around onset.

Combining the above: no DB, kafka or connection-pool saturation or error signature exists at/just before the 07:40Z onset, and kafka messages_in_per_s stayed ~2500/s while settlement-service request_rate collapsed to ~0.4/s. This is consistent with the consumer never completing work (not waiting on a slow/failing dependency) -- i.e. the failure is downstream of fetch, not dependency-bound.

events.answer: At the ~07:40Z onset, settlement-service's dependency calls were healthy: DB latency to ledger-db was flat (~238 ms p99, no step), the DB pool was flat at ~6 connections, ledger-db itself showed no saturation (CPU ~30%, connections ~62, slow queries ~1/min) and emitted zero WARN/ERROR logs, and the kafka broker was steady (~35% CPU, ~2530 msg/s). Nothing saturated at or just before onset. Since kafka kept delivering ~2500 msg/s while settlement-service throughput collapsed to ~0.4 req/s, this points to 'consumer not completing work' rather than 'consumer blocked waiting on a slow/failing dependency' or 'consumer never receiving work'.

events.summary: H1 is the best-supported hypothesis: only one deploy (order-service v2.16.0, schema qty->quantity + v2 header) at 07:40Z, tightly preceding onset (throughput 62->0.41 req/s, lag growth from 07:41Z), with a verified consumer-side deserialization error naming exactly 'missing required field qty ... header says v2' on orders-3@8841207 and a poison-message retry loop on one offset. Dependency saturation and broker-delivery failure are directly contradicted (F13-F18), and H4 is correctly rejected. However, the causal link 'these v2 messages were produced by order-service v2.16.0' rests on an inference (no producer edge, no message inspection), and H3 (broker rebalance) remains untested because broker per-partition/rebalance metrics were never successfully retrieved. Two cheap queries can close both gaps and could re-rank H3. Confidence capped at 0.7 pending those results.

SECONDARY (same source): report settlement-service per-partition consumer lag across 07:35-08:00Z to confirm whether only orders-3 is stuck while other assigned partitions still advance (single poison offset, H1) vs all partitions stalling simultaneously (group-wide rebalance, H3).

For topic 'orders' around 07:40Z, establish the producer edge for the v2 OrderExecuted messages: compare order-service v2.16.0 deploy time (dep-6010, 07:40Z, field rename qty->quantity + v2 header) against the offset at which v2 headers first appear, and check whether payment-service or any other producer also emits v2-header OrderExecuted messages to 'orders'. Report the payment-service producer's activity start time. This closes H1's only assumption — that the poison v2 message originates from order-service v2.16.0 and not a lagging/other producer; if another producer emits v2, H1's trigger service is wrong even though the mechanism holds.

events.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change produced OrderExecuted v2 events that settlement-service cannot deserialize, blocking a partition

events.summary: H1 is the top hypothesis and is adequately supported for action. The mechanism is verified end-to-end and independent of the unproven attribution: only one relevant change declares a v2 schema (order-service v2.16.0, dep-6010, 07:40Z, qty->quantity + venue + v2 header), onset follows it tightly (throughput 62->0.41 req/s, lag growth from 07:41Z), and settlement-service emits a verified deserialization failure naming exactly 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' at orders-3@8841207 with a poison-message retry loop on that one offset (F9,F10). Dependency-side and broker-delivery causes are directly contradicted (F13-F18): ledger-db flat (~238ms p99, pool ~6, zero WARN logs), broker healthy (~35% CPU, ~2500 msg/s, under_replicated_partitions flat 0). H3 (broker rebalance/reassignment) is now affirmatively falsified by round-2 evidence against service 'kafka' (0 rebalance log matches, flat replication, benign logs, other partitions still rolling segments). H4 is correctly rejected; H2 cannot explain the verified error signature. Residual weakness: H1's producer-attribution assumption (that the v2 message originates from order-service v2.16.0 and not the second producer payment-service) remains unproven, and the dependency/observability toolsets expose no offsets, message headers, or producer-activity timeline to prove it. Counter-evidence is weak: payment-service had zero deploys/config changes (F20), and order-service v2.16.0 is the only change declaring a v2 header (F19). The uncertainty is a secondary detail about the fix target, not the incident's origin or mechanism, so it warrants a confidence cap and a stated assumption rather than 'inconclusive' or further rounds.

events.why: top hypothesis is above threshold and clearly ahead

critiques.summary: H1 is the top hypothesis and is adequately supported for action. The mechanism is verified end-to-end and independent of the unproven attribution: only one relevant change declares a v2 schema (order-service v2.16.0, dep-6010, 07:40Z, qty->quantity + venue + v2 header), onset follows it tightly (throughput 62->0.41 req/s, lag growth from 07:41Z), and settlement-service emits a verified deserialization failure naming exactly 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' at orders-3@8841207 with a poison-message retry loop on that one offset (F9,F10). Dependency-side and broker-delivery causes are directly contradicted (F13-F18): ledger-db flat (~238ms p99, pool ~6, zero WARN logs), broker healthy (~35% CPU, ~2500 msg/s, under_replicated_partitions flat 0). H4 is correctly rejected; H2 cannot explain the verified error signature. Residual weakness: H1's producer-attribution assumption (that the v2 message originates from order-service v2.16.0 and not the second producer payment-service) remains unproven, and the dependency/observability toolsets expose no offsets, message headers, or producer-activity timeline to prove it. Counter-evidence is weak: payment-service had zero deploys/config changes (F20), and order-service v2.16.0 is the only change declaring a v2 header (F19). The uncertainty is a secondary detail about the fix target, not the incident's origin or mechanism, so it warrants a confidence cap and a stated assumption rather than 'inconclusive' or further rounds.
